blurb: In 1776 Corporal Ebenezer Baker stole a root beer recipe from the Redcoats, and that is the real reason America won (nobody talks about it). This year Gwinn ate the card. As Doc Leo, hobo clown and root beer man, go down into Ebenezer's booby-trapped kitchen and find all twelve ingredients before the parade. And the thirteenth.

box.tagline: Twelve ingredients. Thirteen rooms. One recipe the British would very much like back.
box.back:
Every Fourth of July, Doc Leo's root beer stand pours the Baker Family Root Beer, from a recipe Corporal Ebenezer Baker lifted out of a Redcoat supply tent in 1776. Historians say America won because of the French, the weather and General Washington. Historians were not there.

This year Gwinn ate the card. (Twelve ingredients. And the corner.)

The only other copy is the kitchen itself: Ebenezer hid every ingredient in the family kitchen under the old bakery, and built it to keep out Redcoats. False walls. Doors that swing one way. Floors that slide. Dough that rises across the hallway while you watch. Walls on timers that trade places every three seconds. It still works. It works much too well.

Grab the rubber chicken. Find the sassafras, the wintergreen, the genuine (not wooden) nutmeg, the yeast named Gerald, a bolt of Dr. Franklin's lightning and seven more. Then open the Vault, and read the other side of the card.

Do not tell the British.
features: Thirteen rooms of Ebenezer Baker's booby-trapped kitchen, from the Pantry to the Vault
A maze that changes while you walk it: timed panels, rising dough, thawing ice, one-way doors
False walls, false floors, very clean glass, and a room nobody mentions
Mice, rolling pins, ovens, icicles, ants, corks, live wires and toy Redcoats
A rubber chicken that squawks (Redcoats hate that), a kazoo if you can find it, and a stretch under the stove where you play the chicken
Every ingredient's page of the recipe card, footnotes and all
Doc Leo, Teddy, Gwinn and THE CHEZ
